findings.summary: GET /api/articles is documented as optional-auth but also declares a 401 response, so anonymous callers may be refused.
GET /api/articles/{slug}/comments is documented as optional-auth yet declares 401, so anonymous reads may be refused.
GET /api/profiles/{username} is documented as optional-auth yet declares 401, so anonymous reads may be refused.
Article list filters tag, author and favorited have no declared response for unknown values (no 404 or empty-result rule), so the outcome for a nonexistent author or username is unsettled.

offset and limit are referenced from shared components whose bounds are not in the source, so the maximum limit, negative offsets and non-numeric values are unverified and no upper bound is stated anywhere.
Token lifetime and post-expiry behaviour are not stated; the token description gives issuance but no expiry or revocation rule.
Duplicate username or email is covered for sign-up (409) but PUT /api/user declares no 409, so a conflicting update has no defined outcome.
Article create returns 409 for a conflict but PUT /api/articles/{slug} declares no 409, although a changed title may produce a clashing slug.
Favouriting an already-favourited article and following an already-followed author have no declared 409 or idempotent outcome; the same applies to unfavourite and unfollow when not in that state.

Ownership rules return 403 for non-owners on edit, delete and comment-delete, but nothing settles whether a non-owner gets 403 or 404 for a resource they cannot see, and the spec lacks a 403 for comment creation.
Following oneself is not covered: the follow route declares no 4xx for a self-follow attempt.
Comment id is typed integer, but a non-integer id, or an id belonging to another article, has no stated status (422 or 404).
GET /api/tags declares a 422 response although it takes no input, so the source of that error is not explained.
